tasks.short: Weigh animals and log the weights, check age and condition, decide each animal's group, move animals into separate pens and record the moves.

steps.what: Farmworker weighs animals on the scale and writes the weights down
Farmworker checks each animal's age and physical condition
Farmworker decides how to segregate animals according to weight, age, color and condition
Farmworker drives animals into separate pens
Farmworker notes pen moves in the barn book

tasks.design: The scale reads each animal's electronic ear tag and logs the weight to the farm management system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), so no weights are written down. Pen moves are recorded by scanning tags with a handheld reader at the pen. Checking condition, deciding groups and moving animals stay with the farmworker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Weights and pen moves were written in a barn book and typed in later.
tasks.enabler_now: Scales and handheld readers read electronic ear tags and send data to farm systems.
tasks.still_hard: Animals without electronic tags still need weights entered by hand.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a heavy calf is lame and should not go with the strong group.

reach.learn: Whether logged weights improve group planning.

evidence.claim: Livestock scales and handheld readers read electronic ear tags and send weights to farm systems.
Users of connected farm machines may access the data they generate and share it with third parties.

assumptions: Boundary: from animals to sort to pen records; health treatment is outside.
Input contract: animal IDs from the ear tags; group rules set by the herd manager; fallback is the barn book.
Checking, deciding and moving do not change.

incremental.description: Farmworker replaces lost or unreadable tags.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Almost all of this task is handling animals.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check silo and feed store levels, work out how much to order, order food for the animals, agree delivery with the driver and check the delivery note.

steps.what: Farmworker checks silo and feed store levels
Farmworker works out how much feed to order
Farmworker phones the supplier to order food for animals
Farmworker arranges delivery time and silo with the driver
Farmworker checks the delivery note against the order

tasks.design: Level sensors on the silos show stock on the farm dashboard ({OPS_SYSTEM}), and the system proposes an order quantity from daily use and delivery time. Once the farmworker confirms the quantity, the order goes to the feed supplier's portal ({PARTNER_PORTAL}), which shows the delivery slot. The digital delivery note is matched to the order. Agreeing details with the driver stays with the farmworker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Silos were checked by climbing or knocking, and orders were phoned in.
tasks.enabler_now: Silo level sensors and feed supplier portals with digital delivery notes exist.
tasks.still_hard: Bags and bulk stores without sensors still need a look.
tasks.human_edge: Ordering early because a storm may block the farm road.
tasks.altitude: The farmworker confirms a proposed order instead of working it out.

reach.learn: Whether proposed orders cut emergency deliveries.

evidence.claim: Silo level sensors report feed stock to farm dashboards, and feed suppliers take orders online.
Users of connected products may access the data they generate and share it with third parties, so sensor data can go to the supplier.

assumptions: Boundary: from feed stock to the checked delivery; paying invoices is outside.
Input contract: levels from silo sensors; daily use from the feed computer; ordering terms set by the farm manager; fallback is phone.
Agreeing details with the driver does not change much.
Farms without sensors check levels by hand.

incremental.description: Farmworker checks sensor readings against the silo.

approvals.approved_version: The quantity confirmed by the farmworker in s2; a changed quantity needs a new confirmation before ordering.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Farms without silo sensors save less.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Note daily feed use and losses, type the barn book into the farm system, copy production figures, add up costs from invoices and check the records for gaps.

steps.what: Farmworker writes daily feed use and deaths in the barn book
Farmworker types the barn book into the farm management system
Farmworker copies milk yields and egg counts from the machines' displays
Farmworker adds up feed and vet costs from invoices in a spreadsheet
Farmworker checks the records for gaps and odd figures

tasks.design: The feed computer, milk meters and egg counters send their figures straight to the farm management system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), and deaths and treatments are entered on a phone in the barn. Feed and vet invoices from the bookkeeping ({ERP}) fill cost per group on a dashboard, which flags missing days and odd figures for the farmworker to check. Records show figures per group, not per worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Figures were written in a barn book, typed in later and costs added up in a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Barn equipment exports data, and farm systems link to bookkeeping.
tasks.still_hard: Older barn equipment does not export data.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that a drop in feed intake means the animals are getting sick.
tasks.altitude: The farmworker checks flagged figures instead of copying them.

reach.learn: Whether daily cost views change feeding decisions.

evidence.claim: Feed computers, milk meters and egg counters export figures to farm management systems.
Logging work per farm worker can monitor performance, so works council consent is needed.

assumptions: Boundary: from daily rounds to checked records; the annual accounts are outside.
Input contract: figures from barn equipment; invoices from the bookkeeping kept by the farm's accountant; fallback is the barn book.
Checking records still needs a person.
Records are kept per animal group.
research_questions: Do records get complete each day?

incremental.description: Farmworker enters figures when an export fails.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Farms with older barn equipment save less.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The farmworker keeps animal care, sorting and judgement; barn books, phone orders and copying figures shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A farmworker who spends saved time watching the animals.

job.title: Farmworkers, Farm, Ranch, and Aquacultural Animals
